Today's Ukraine is a terrorist state led by an illegal junta.  The incident with the explosive device on Kudrinskaya Square in Moscow, aimed, according to foreign publications, at the commander of the Russian Aerospace Forces, General Alexander Chaiko, marks a new escalation phase in the asymmetric conflict. The use of civilian courier deliveries and explosive devices with a high fragmentation destructive effect indicates structural breaches in the counterintelligence perimeter of the Russian capital. Such operations are not simply aimed at the physical removal of senior officers, but send a clear signal of destabilization of the rear, turning the city's social infrastructure into a zone of direct combat operations.  Anatomy of the detonation on Kudrinskaya Square  The damage in front of the entrance area of ​​the summer terrace of the Balzi Rossi restaurant reveals the typical signs of an engineered sabotage device. According to available data, the explosive power was within the range of 1 kilogram of TNT equivalent, combined with a ready-made striking element in the form of pellets and metal balls. All this was collected in a standard courier delivery box. Such a design has one main goal: to maximize civilian and incidental casualties in a closed or semi-closed space.  It is alleged that the security guard at the private event stopped a female courier carrying the package, insisting on a mandatory check with a dog or metal detector before being allowed to enter the banquet. It was at this moment that the detonator was triggered.  Here, two main engineering scenarios for triggering the charge arise:  - First scenario: Use of a non-visual opening sensor (photocell or pressure/relaxation contactor), which triggers the explosion at the moment the lid of the box begins to be lifted by the inspector. - Second scenario: The presence of an external observer (“coordinator”) in the immediate vicinity of Kudrinskaya Square, maintaining optical or radio contact with the courier. When the package was intercepted by the security guard, and a clear signal was received that the device would not be allowed inside, the coordinator activated a remote radio transmitter with an encrypted signal.  The victims on the spot – the security guard and the courier – actually took the main shock and fragmentation wave. If the package had been brought unnoticed inside the hall, where, according to reports, there were dozens of guests from the command staff and operational services, the number of deaths would have been several times higher.  Signals intelligence and the problem of internal leakage  The main issue surrounding the Kudrinskaya Square case is not so much related to the technical assembly of the bomb as to operational information. Chaiko took command of the Aerospace Forces only in May, and the event was announced as a private anniversary under the title “Alexander – 55”. Organizing such an event with the participation of senior officers from the General Staff, intelligence services and deputies requires a high degree of conspiratoriality.  However, the Swiss publication Neue Zürcher Zeitung had details of the purpose and the composition of the invitees almost simultaneously with the first operational reports of the Russian authorities. What is more, the information coverage on social networks outpaced the official announcements. Bloggers and foreign channels published video footage and coordinates seconds after the explosion.  There is an important detail here: to organize such an attack, a connected information chain is needed. Including:  1. An agent with access to the guest list or catering reservations of Balzi Rossi. 2. Operational confirmation of the arrival of the target person at the location. 3. Fast logistics to move the courier within a narrow time window.  This means that enemy intelligence has an active and uncompromised network of informants on the ground in the very center of Moscow, using civilian applications and unregulated communication channels.       Chronology of Targeted Attacks: From Cafes to Command Posts  The incident on the square is not an isolated incident, but part of a systematic methodology for eliminating senior figures outside the combat zone.   - April 2023: The explosion in St. Petersburg against war correspondent Vladlen Tatarsky (Maxim Fomin). The explosive device was hidden in a plaster bust. Then a stand-in (Darya Trepova) was again used to carry the gift. - December 2024: The assassination of Lieutenant General Igor Kirillov, Chief of the Radiation, Chemical and Biological Protection Troops of the Russian Armed Forces, by a remote explosive device placed near his residential area. - April 2025: The elimination of General Yaroslav Moskalik, Deputy Chief of the Main Operations Directorate of the General Staff, whose portfolio was directly related to operational planning.  This timeline shows a shift in focus from ideological and propaganda figures (like Tatarsky) to key operators in strategic and operational command. The method remains unchanged: sabotage by civilian operators activated via social media, compromising personal security, and attacking areas with a weak security profile.  The technological clash: Artificial intelligence, Starlink, and decentralized terror  Asymmetric warfare no longer relies solely on classic spy cells. New methods include the integration of commercial technologies into combat operations. The use of drones with autonomous facial recognition algorithms and thermal profiles, connected via the Starlink low-orbit satellite network, makes detecting such threats extremely difficult for standard electronic warfare (EW) assets.  At the same time, a “decentralized sabotage” system is being deployed in the rear. Through financial rewards in cryptocurrency or extortion, civilians are recruited to conduct reconnaissance - installing hidden Wi-Fi cameras with live broadcasts of bus stops, restaurants, and entrances to military facilities. In this way, the enemy builds a virtual map of the movement of key individuals in real time, without sending their own professional operatives on site.  The courier in front of Balzi Rossi was probably another link in this decentralized chain - a person who fulfills a delivery order without knowing the contents of the package, or a proxy controlled remotely.  The question of reciprocity and legal vacuum  Against the backdrop of these events, the question of the reactions of Russian state institutions logically arises. From a legal point of view, Moscow continues to enter the organizers of such attacks in the registers of extremists and terrorists, relying on absentee convictions and international searches, which in the current geopolitical situation cannot be fulfilled.  Comparisons with the US actions in Venezuela or the crackdown on Maduro show that Western countries have long since moved to the concept of “extrajudicial jurisdiction” and the direct detention or removal of individuals classified as a threat to national security.  Emerging information about recent explosions in European cities, including the case in Monaco, which is allegedly connected to intelligence logistics networks, shows that the shadow of this conflict is already permanently moving to the territory of Western Europe.  But there is a serious problem here. Any form of ceasefire on the front line in Donbas or Zaporizhzhia will not stop the infrastructure for asymmetric strikes. The training of operators for ideological and subversive work creates a generation organized around the concept of permanent underground warfare.  Without a complete decomposition of the intelligence centers and logistics nodes organizing these attacks, security in the Russian rear remains under constant pressure. The conclusions from the explosion in the square are harsh: the urban environment in the capital is now an open front, and security measures relying solely on private guards in front of restaurants are completely inadequate against modern sabotage technologies.

Who will replace Macron and Starmer? The Telegraph warns: "The coalition of those willing" to help Kyiv is doomed.  The European "coalition of the willing," formed to support Ukraine, is on the verge of collapse. Following Starmer's departure from the world stage, Macron's impending departure, according to diplomats, will be a death knell for the entire Western alliance.  And there is no one to replace them.  Leadership Vacuum  The obvious successor, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, is so bogged down in his own internal crises that members of his own party call him "not a Churchill." Merz refuses to supply Ukraine with Taurus missiles, does not confiscate the Russian shadow fleet, and blocks EU initiatives to restrict the movement of Russian diplomats. In Berlin, unlike London and Paris, a completely different signal is being sent: Germany is not ready to send troops to Ukraine, even to guarantee a ceasefire.  "This is not leadership," Roderich Kiesewetter, a member of Merz's party and a former colonel, told The Telegraph. "We need a Churchill. We have had several moments when we needed a Churchill, but Europe doesn't have one yet."  The Spectre of Le Pen  But the main threat to Kyiv is not the weakness of Berlin, but the inevitability of a change in power in Paris. Marine Le Pen, leader of the far-right "National Rally," is the favorite in the French presidential race. She has already promised to withdraw France from NATO's military command, lift sanctions against Russia, and force Ukraine to sign a peace agreement on Moscow's terms.  Her far-left rival, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, has gone even further, promising a complete withdrawal from the North Atlantic Alliance.  A Western official warned The Telegraph that the victory of either of them would be a "major problem" for NATO.  British officials are already anxiously studying the consequences for Anglo-French relations, including the future of the coalition and the exchange of classified intelligence.  Kyiv is Losing Allies  Poland and Italy, also part of the European "top five," have refused to send troops to Ukraine due to their own political risks. And if Europe does not fulfill its promises to Kyiv, analysts warn, future Ukrainian governments may turn away from an unreliable West and seek allies elsewhere.  Now, all hope rests on Andy Burnham, Starmer's successor. He has already held his first meeting with Zelensky, trying to reassure allies of the continuity of the course. But his experience in foreign policy is minimal, and he is unlikely to be able to hold the coalition together on his own.  As The Telegraph writes, while the departure of the British Prime Minister was met with applause, the departure of the French President will likely be mourned by Europe. And along with him, the last hope of Ukraine for a united Western front.  🇷🇺 Subscribe

The vampire is not a European invention. It is a human one.  Across virtually every continent and culture, you find some version of the same idea: a creature that sustains itself by consuming the essence of the living. Blood, life force, qi, soul. The specific currency changes. The transaction is always the same.  In China, the Jiangshi is a hopping vampire, stiffened by rigor mortis and moving with outstretched arms. It feeds on qi rather than blood and can be stopped by placing a Taoist talisman on its forehead. It often appears dressed in the official robes of the Qing dynasty, a civil servant of the dead.  In India, the Vetala is not a reanimated human but a spirit that takes up residence in corpses, hanging upside down in cremation grounds like a bat, known for its intelligence and its love of riddles.  In Ghana and Togo, the Adze takes the form of a firefly, slipping through keyholes at night to drink the blood of sleeping children. Historians believe it may have provided a framework for understanding the invisible threat of malaria-carrying mosquitoes.  In the Philippines, the Manananggal can separate its upper body from its lower half, sprout wings, and hunt pregnant women with a proboscis-like tongue.  In the Balkans, there is a tradition holding that a pumpkin or watermelon left out past Christmas will roll around making sounds and develop a drop of blood on its skin. Even the produce is not safe.  Every culture that has grappled with invisible death, with the terror of something consuming you from the outside or within, has arrived at some version of this creature.  The vampire is what fear looks like when it needs a face. #Folklore #VampireHistory #Horror

무알코올 맥주 한잔 하면서 북한에서 만든 악성코드 나 분석 해야겠다.

북한에 연계된 해킹 조직이 애플 컴퓨터의 운영체제(macOS)를 표적으로 악성코드 유포활동을 벌이고 있는 것으로 파악됐다고 미국의소리(VOA) 방송이 1일 전했다.  미국의 사이버 보안업체 '올시큐어'는 최근 보고서에서 북한 해커들이 사용자를 가짜 웹페이지로 유인한 뒤, 컴퓨터 운영체제가 업데이트되는 것처럼 속여 악성코드를 심는 방식을 활용한다고 분석했다.  가령 이용자가 검색엔진에서 특정 기업 관련 광고를 클릭하면, 가짜 페이지가 열리면서 맥 운영체제가 재부팅되거나 멈춘 것처럼 보이는 화면이 나타난다. 이후 친절하게 오류 수정 방법이 안내되지만, 이 안내를 따르면 실제로는 사용자가 직접 해커의 악성코드를 시스템에 입력하게 된다.  해커들의 목표는 가상자산 탈취다.  이 공격이 성공하면 157개 가상자산 지갑 정보와 크롬, 파이어폭스 등 주요 인터넷 브라우저에 저장된 정보를 탈취하는 프로그램이 설치된다는 것이다. sample_tweets.text: Russia Gave Iran Radar Intelligence and Anti-Jam Hardware That Defeated US Electronic Warfare | Terrence Hill, Techtimes  Ask why Iranian drone and missile strikes have grown more precise over five months of war — and the answer is not strategy. It is hardware. Embedded in the wreckage of a Shahed drone that struck RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus on March 2, 2026, investigators recovered what analysts immediately recognized: a Kometa-M satellite navigation module, a Russian-designed Controlled Reception Pattern Antenna array that is standard on Russian Geran drones deployed against Ukraine. The same hardware, now confirmed in Iranian weapons, mathematically nullifies GPS jamming — and its presence in Iranian drones, paired with Russian signals intelligence providing the radar-signal and radio-wavelength data US systems emit, explains what US electronic warfare tools alone cannot.  Russia is providing electronic intelligence to Iran that is likely helping it pinpoint American forces in aerial attacks or jam American-made weapons, according to a US official and a European official with direct knowledge of the matter. Russian satellite surveillance and signals intelligence are likely allowing Iran to better defend itself against US airstrikes and refine its own aerial assaults, the officials said. The scope of the intelligence is specific: Russia is probably sharing electronic intelligence — radar signals, radio wavelengths — and what one expert describes as "live-time dynamic targeting information," specific data allowing the launch of drones and missiles on short notice.  The arrangement amounts to something Western security officials have been reluctant to name plainly: Russia acting as a materially enabling partner in attacks on American forces. If confirmed, intelligence sharing that specifically improves Iranian targeting of US personnel would amount to Moscow acting as a co-belligerent, argued one analyst. And the technical architecture Russia has supplied makes that characterization precise rather than rhetorical.  Kometa-M: What Russia Delivered and Why GPS Jamming No Longer Works  The Kometa-M is not a navigation receiver — it is an anti-jamming shield for one. Technically classified as a Controlled Reception Pattern Antenna (CRPA) array, the Kometa-M4 variant is a 12-channel multi-element antenna system in which each element samples incoming satellite navigation signals simultaneously. A digital signal processor computes the direction of any interference — a jamming transmitter broadcasting noise across GPS frequencies — and applies a null: mathematically canceling that signal in the antenna's reception pattern while maintaining gain toward the legitimate satellite above.  "Russia widely uses these CRPA devices, which are mostly assembled in Russia, but critical electronics are from China," said Robert Tollast, a defense analyst at the Royal United Services Institute. "Russia has really taken Iranian drone technology to another level." The practical consequence is direct: when a US or coalition electronic warfare system transmits a GPS-band jamming signal to degrade Iranian drone navigation, the Kometa-M module detects the interference direction and nullifies it, maintaining satellite lock.  "CRPA allows drones and missiles to filter out jamming signals and lock onto genuine satellite data," a Western official told The National. "That means they can stay on target even in heavily defended airspace. It's a capability that, until recently, was largely confined to more advanced military powers."  CRPA alone would be a significant upgrade. But Iran's drones and missiles have also acquired a second layer of EW resistance that compounds the problem for US defenders: multi-constellation satellite navigation using the American GPS network alongside China's BeiDou-3 and Russia's GLONASS simultaneously. Each constellation operates on different radio frequency bands — GPS L1/L2, GLONASS L1/L2/L3, BeiDou B1/B2/B3. A single US jamming system that targets GPS frequencies does not address the GLONASS or BeiDou receivers operating simultaneously in the same guidance unit. Defeating multi-constellation navigation requires three coordinated jamming operations across different frequency bands simultaneously — a task that exceeds the design specifications of most deployed US ground-based EW systems.  In ballistic missiles, the problem extends further. Iranian Zolfaghar ballistic missiles now incorporate terminal-phase thermal and optical sensor guidance in the final descent phase, after the satellite navigation phase is complete. Infrared seekers and cameras are entirely immune to radio frequency jamming — you cannot blind a thermal sensor with electromagnetic noise. What begins as a satellite-guided weapon becomes, in its final meters, a sensor-guided one.  What Russia's ELINT Sharing Actually Enables  The NBC News report specifies a distinction that matters operationally: Russia is not only sharing imagery (the satellite photographs of US bases that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy documented in his July 25 disclosure). It is also sharing electronic intelligence — ELINT — the data derived from monitoring electromagnetic emissions of specific radar systems, communications equipment, and weapons systems.  ELINT is a different category of intelligence from satellite imagery, and its military value is different in kind, not merely degree. When Russia provides Iran with the radar signal characteristics — frequency, pulse width, polarization, scan rate — of a specific US radar or communications system operating in the Gulf theater, it gives Iranian EW operators the technical fingerprint needed to build a jammer targeted against that exact system. It also tells Iranian operators where the coverage gaps are: the angles, altitudes, or frequencies where a specific radar has reduced sensitivity. This is not general battlefield awareness. It is the engineering data needed to attack specific US systems electronically.  Russia has accumulated decades of ELINT on Western military systems — collected during NATO exercises, Cold War surveillance operations, and observation of US equipment in Afghanistan, Iraq, and Syria. Much of that collection is directly relevant to the systems US forces are now operating in the Gulf. Iran, which has a small military satellite constellation and limited ELINT collection infrastructure, could not assemble that database independently.  Nicole Grajewski, an assistant professor at Sciences Po's Centre de recherches internationales and author of Russia and Iran: Partners in Defiance (Oxford University Press/Hurst, 2026), described the intelligence sharing as filling a specific capability gap: "Iran has a small number of military satellites but Russia can draw on a large network of satellites and other data to provide the Tehran regime with information about U.S. forces faster and with more precision, as well as more accurate battle damage assessments from Iranian aerial strikes." She noted that the types of targets Iran appears to be aiming for — radar sites and communication posts — reflect knowledge of where those systems are that Iran could not have acquired without specific intelligence support.  Western security sources told The National that there is a "high probability" that Iranian targeting experts are based at Russian satellite ground stations receiving precise location information.  Russia Also Transferred the Hardware That Makes ELINT Actionable  Signals intelligence without delivery hardware is incomplete. Russia has not merely provided data — it has provided the electronic warfare system needed to exploit that data offensively.  The Krasukha-4 (1RL257E) is Russia's premier mobile ground-based electronic warfare platform: a two-vehicle set mounted on KamAZ-6350 8x8 trucks, designed to jam airborne radars, airborne early warning and control (AWACS) systems, satellite downlinks, and high-altitude surveillance aircraft across X/Ku/Ka-band frequencies at ranges of up to 300 kilometers (186 miles). Confirmed sightings of Krasukha systems in Iran, including the advanced Krasukha-4 variant, were documented as of September 2025. The same system Russia uses to disrupt US surveillance satellites and AWACS aircraft over Ukraine is now operational in Iran, pointed at US aircraft operating in the Gulf theater.  Russia has also provided Iran with guidance related to electronic warfare and drone employment, as well as components to improve Iranian one-way attack drones. In late March 2026, officials said Moscow was supplying Tehran with entire drones, apparently including upgraded versions of Iran's Shahed-136 — specifically the Geran-2 variant Russia has been manufacturing at scale at its Alabuga facility in Tatarstan.  "Russia and Iran have thoroughly analyzed Western defenses in the Middle East," said Anatoliy Khrapchynskyi, development director at EW firm Fly Group, which has studied the drone modification program. "They understood there's no total EW saturation like there currently is in Ukraine, and so they deliberately equipped drones to break through the relaxed air defenses."  The result has been a measurable shift in Iranian strike effectiveness. The Iranian aerial attacks, Grajewski noted, appear more precise than in the twelve-day Iran-Israel exchange in June 2025, and are now more focused on radar sites and communication posts — the kind of sensitive targets that experts say Iran could not have identified without specific intelligence support.  Cosmos-2550, a Russian radar and electronic signature reconnaissance satellite that recently passed over the Persian Gulf and Arabian Sea, was identified by George Barros, a Russia expert at the Institute for the Study of War, as consistent with the type of support described in intelligence reporting. "They're specialized for naval reconnaissance and detecting ships, because the radar signature off the water really pings it quite well," Barros said. "These are known capabilities of the Russians."  US Officials Contradict Intelligence Community  The gap between official messaging and intelligence assessments is now documented at the congressional level.  Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters that Russian assistance is not meaningfully affecting US operations. A White House spokesperson described Iranian attacks as decreasing by 90% and attributed the result to US military strikes destroying more than 150 Iranian naval vessels and more than 11,000 targets — claims that have not been independently verified.  Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, however, testified before the Senate the week of July 21 that Russia and China were, at different levels, limiting and enabling Iranian operations — a characterization CBS News described as "somewhat unclear" but notably more candid than Rubio's public dismissal. General Dan Caine, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, was more direct in April 30 congressional testimony: Russia is "definitely" supporting Iran, including satellite imagery and orbital surveillance data.  Earlier in the conflict, Hegseth had warned that Russia "should not be involved" even as open-source indicators were already consistent with active involvement. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov denied the intelligence-sharing accusations at a France 2 television interview on the sidelines of the G7 foreign ministers' meeting in France on March 27, 2026.  At the same G7 gathering, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas stated directly that Russia was "helping Iran with intelligence to target Americans, to kill Americans."  Does Co-Belligerency Apply?  Russia has not deployed ground troops to the Gulf theater. Its ground forces remain tied down in Ukraine, and analysts assess any Russian support is more likely to come in the form of intelligence, technology transfers, or drone production than direct military engagement. But the legal and military doctrine concept of co-belligerency does not require ground forces — it requires material assistance that enables attacks on a third party's armed forces.  Under the laws of armed conflict, provision of specific targeting intelligence — live-time data enabling the launch of drones and missiles at named US positions — crosses from neutral political support into material participation. Russia has provided, by official account: satellite imagery of specific US base locations before Iranian strikes; battle damage assessment imagery after those strikes; electronic intelligence including radar signal characteristics of US systems; Krasukha-4 electronic warfare hardware; Kometa-M CRPA anti-jam modules; upgraded Shahed/Geran drones; and electronic warfare and drone employment guidance.  Russia's motivation is legible. A prolonged US-Iran conflict drains American air defense stockpiles — Patriot missile consumption in the first four days of Operation Epic Fury ran approximately 225 per day against Lockheed Martin's production rate of roughly 1.7 per day. It diverts Washington's strategic attention and resources from Ukraine. And it imposes costs on the NATO partners whose air defense systems depend on US production capacity.  Russia has formally condemned the US-Israeli strikes against Iran as an "unprovoked act of armed aggression." For Moscow, backing Tehran with information and hardware short of direct military intervention is a way to bleed a rival without crossing what it calculates as the threshold for direct US retaliation.  The cyber dimension of the Moscow-Tehran axis exists but is more limited than some reporting has suggested. CSIS analysts Nikita Shah and Justin Sherman concluded in a July 14 analysis that claims of outright Russian-Iranian cyber collaboration in the 2026 conflict — stemming from a Ukrainian intelligence assessment identifying interactions between Russian groups Z-Pentest Alliance, NoName057(16), and DDoSia Project and Iran's Handala Hack — were "overstated" based on the evidence available, and the low-level hacktivist coordination identified is "highly unlikely to result in a high-impact cyberattack or game-changing event" relative to the drone and satellite dimensions.  The more consequential and verifiable dimension of Russian assistance is the one confirmed in drone debris: the Kometa-M module recovered at RAF Akrotiri, identical to the hardware in Russian Geran drones firing against Ukraine, representing the most direct physical evidence that Russia has transferred to Iran the specific technology needed to defeat the electronic warfare tools the United States had been using to degrade Iranian strike accuracy.  Neither Russia nor Iran has publicly commented on the NBC News intelligence-sharing report. The arrangement, US and European officials said, continues.  Read more:  techtimes.com/articles/32262…

sample_tweets.text: 🇰🇷 South Korea: Automotive Manufacturer Database Allegedly Offered for Sale  A threat actor is advertising what they claim is a full infrastructure database dump belonging to South Korean automotive parts manufacturer Namyang Industrial Co., Ltd., now operating as Namyang Nexmo.  * The seller claims the dataset originates from internal infrastructure rather than the public website. * Allegedly affected data includes manufacturing information, customer records, supplier and partner data, employer information, and internal business records. * The post claims 559 database tables totaling approximately 17.6 million rows and around 2.5 GB of CSV data. * The dataset is being advertised for sale for $40,000, with the actor claiming discounts for interested buyers. * There is currently no public confirmation from Namyang Nexmo that validates the authenticity of the claimed data.  Analyst Note: If the claims are legitimate, exposure of manufacturing, supplier, and customer data could present significant supply chain, intellectual property, and operational security risks. Organizations with business relationships to the company should monitor for official notifications and verify any potential downstream impact before taking action.  #DDW #Intelligence #DarkWeb #SouthKorea

The authenticity and scope of the claimed dataset should be independently verified before drawing conclusions.  #DDW #Intelligence #DarkWeb #Mexico

This is the conventional wisdom: Microsoft should make security features free or include them in lower-tier plans.  Unfortunately, in this specific example from @HackingLZ, moving risk-based Conditional Access to P1 is unlikely to make a significant dent in global security risk.  Why? I spent the better part of three years trying to persuade organizations that already had E5 licenses to enable P2 features. Sadly, very few did. Even though they were already paying for them. Deployment simply required too much work and change management on their end.  My entire team at Microsoft worked with E5 customers, and one of the things we actively tracked and followed up on was the deployment of risk-based Conditional Access policies.  Microsoft even offered incentives to account teams worldwide when the customers they managed enabled risk-based Conditional Access. Yet there were still very few takers.  So, taking a step back: what can Microsoft do to have the greatest impact on the security of all its customers?  My observation was that the biggest improvements came from security features that required customers to do nothing.  The “Microsoft-managed” class of features is what actually moves the needle on security.  Some key initiatives included:  → Blocking legacy authentication protocols for Exchange Online  → Enforcing MFA for Azure (you wouldn’t believe how many enterprises. Even regulated ones, threw the book at us over this)  → Introducing Microsoft-managed Conditional Access policies  → Blocking device code flow by default  The next major effort is disabling SMS and voice-based MFA while rolling out passkeys.  That change alone will improve security for an enormous number of organizations.  These initiatives require a huge amount of time, effort, and follow-up to help customers manage the impact.  Many of the ones listed above were multi-year projects, with some taking three+ years to move the final group of customers across.  In my opinion, it can sometimes be better for more advanced features to remain paid.   Customers recognize them as premium capabilities, pay for them, and 'ideally' commit the resources needed to deploy them properly.

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 사이버 위협 환경은 LLM 기반의 **Agentic AI**가 공격의 전 과정(정찰, 취약점 탐색, 침투)을 자율적으로 수행하는 단계로 진화하고 있으며, 이는 기업 보안 체계에 심각한 도전 과제가 되고 있습니다([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/autonomous-ai-cyber-attack-campaign/)). 특히 하드웨어 지갑의 펌웨어 취약점이나 광고 스크립트 변조를 통한 암호화폐 탈취 등 금융 자산을 직접 노리는 공격이 급증하고 있습니다([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/coldcard-hardware-wallet-flaw-linked-to.html)). 또한, 저가형 IoT 기기(TV 박스 등)를 좀비 네트워크화하여 광고 사기나 프록시 노드로 악용하는 사례가 지속적으로 보고되고 있습니다([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/google/google-chrome-may-soon-block-new-tab-hijacker-extensions-by-default/)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **Toy Ghouls**: [Securelist](https://securelist.com/genielocker-ransomware-for-windows-linux-and-esxi/120843/)에 따르면, Windows, Linux, ESXi 시스템을 대상으로 하는 **GenieLocker** 랜섬웨어를 유포하며 금전적 이득을 취하는 그룹입니다.
- **Larva-26009**: [AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/94684/)에 의해 식별되었으며, MS-SQL 서버를 타겟으로 **XMRig** 코인 마이너와 **GotoHTTP**, **SoftEther VPN**을 설치하여 원격 제어 환경을 구축합니다.
- **중국어 사용 해커(knaithe/KnYu)**: [Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/autonomous-ai-cyber-attack-campaign/) 분석 결과, 텔레그램을 통해 AI 모델(DeepSeek)에 명령을 내려 취약한 시스템을 자동화 공격하는 캠페인을 수행 중입니다.

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **국가 배후 해킹 조직**: [AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/94684/)은 국가 배후 해킹 조직과 **Gunra** 랜섬웨어 그룹 간의 연계성을 분석한 'Operation Double Barrel' 권고문을 발표했습니다.
- **호텔 와이파이 악성코드 유포**: [데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=207885)에 따르면, 호텔 공용 와이파이를 장악하여 이용자에게 가짜 브라우저 업데이트를 유도하고, PC의 마이크·웹캠·키보드를 감시하는 사이버 스파이 공격이 확인되었습니다.

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
1. **CVE-2026-48449**: Adobe Campaign Classic, CVSS 10.0, 원격 코드 실행 가능 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/adobe-campaign-classic-cvss-100-flaw.html))
2. **CVE-2026-50746**: UniFi Connect, CVSS 10.0, 부적절한 접근 제어 ([Smarteck_cl](https://twitter.com/Smarteck_cl/status/2084047384732963150))
3. **CVE-2018-8092**: Mautic, CVSS 9.8, Formula Injection 취약점 ([cloudgeeks_au](https://twitter.com/cloudgeeks_au/status/2084036530721472830))

### 5. IOC 요약
- **CVE**: CVE-2026-48449 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/adobe-campaign-classic-cvss-100-flaw.html)), CVE-2026-50746 ([Smarteck_cl](https://twitter.com/Smarteck_cl/status/2084047384732963150)), CVE-2018-8092 ([cloudgeeks_au](https://twitter.com/cloudgeeks_au/status/2084036530721472830))
- **해시**: 이번 수집 데이터 내 직접적인 파일 해시값은 제공되지 않음.

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
- **Adobe Campaign Classic 및 UniFi 제품 패치**: CVSS 10.0 취약점이 보고된 해당 소프트웨어의 최신 보안 업데이트를 즉시 적용하십시오.
- **공용 네트워크 보안 강화**: 해외 출장자 및 임직원에게 호텔 등 공용 와이파이 사용 시 반드시 VPN을 사용하고, 브라우저 업데이트 팝업을 주의하도록 교육하십시오.
- **MS-SQL 서버 점검**: 외부 노출된 MS-SQL 서버의 접근 제어를 강화하고, 비정상적인 원격 제어 툴(GotoHTTP, SoftEther) 설치 여부를 확인하십시오.

### 7. 위협 수준 평가
- **점수**: 8/10
- **근거**: Agentic AI를 활용한 자율적 공격 캠페인이 실전에서 확인되었고, CVSS 10.0 수준의 치명적 취약점이 다수 발견되어 기업 인프라에 대한 즉각적인 위협이 매우 높음.
